title: Sundial handoff: evening scrub, escalations, and runbook deltas
content:
Quick summary:
- Shift: evening (US-west peaked traffic window), 16:50-00:00 PDT handover.
- Primary event: intermittent 95th-pct latency spike for text-generation endpoints (hosted-api /v1/generate) between ~18:10 and 18:40 PDT on 2028-03-29.
- Impact: elevated tail latency (p95 from 210ms -> 1.8s), increased request timeouts, ~2% error-rate bump for a 30-minute window. Affected customers were on the hosted tier in us-west-2 region; Dedicated customers unaffected.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): aggressive kv-cache eviction after a config rollout (cache_shards=16 -> 8) combined with autoscaler oscillation causing reaped workers to rehydrate KV caches, which amplified latency under bursty traffic.

Timeline (short):
- 18:07 PDT - Alert: latency anomaly (alert:service:hosted-p95-latency) triggered.
- 18:10 PDT - SRE oncall (Maya) started triage, confirmed p95 and error-rate rise.
- 18:15 PDT - On-call opened INC-2028-03-29-17 and paged infra (Luca).
- 18:20 PDT - Observed node-level OOM-swap churn on a subset of g4dn-16xlarge hosts; autoscaler triggered scale-down then immediate scale-up (reclaim threshold tuned incorrectly for burstiness).
- 18:28 PDT - Applied mitigation: temporarily set cache_shards back to 16 on canary pool and enabled conservative autoscaler (scale_down_delay increased to 300s).
- 18:33 PDT - p95 reduced toward baseline; by 18:45 PDTevent considered contained.
- 18:50 PDT - Post-mortem triage started; initial notes captured below.

Actions taken during shift (operational):
- Reverted cache_shards change on canary pool (rollback, see PR#834).
- Increased autoscaler scale_down_delay to 300s cluster-wide as temporary guard.
- Restarted 6 worker processes on pool-03 that showed repeated cache rehydrate latency spikes (rolling restart, no traffic loss due to draining).
- Elevated metric retention for kv_cache_hit_ratio and worker_rehydrate_duration to 1h resolution for the next 48h to aid analysis.

Observations / signals we tracked:
- KV cache hit ratio dropped from ~0.92 to 0.41 during spike window.
- Worker rehydrate duration histogram 99th jumped to ~1.2s for rehydrations >1MB KV payloads.
- Autoscaler logs show scale-down triggers at T1 and scale-up at T1+30s — too reactive for bursty seq distribution.
- Memory footprint on affected nodes increased after rollback but stabilized once rehydrations finished.

Runbook delta (draft) - immediate edits to SRE Runbook (short term):
- Add explicit step: when p95 > 1s and kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.7, prioritize cache policy rollback to canary and set autoscaler to conservative mode (scale_down_delay >= 300s).
- Add commands snippet: 
  - kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/worker-pool-03 --context=us-west-2
  - curl -XPOST https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/cache/policy -d '{"shards":16}' (auth: svc-sre-key)
- Add diagnostics: how to pull worker_rehydrate_duration histogram + node memory metrics (grafana dashboards and queries included in Confluence runbook link).
- Add post-rollback verification checklist (p95, kv_cache_hit_ratio, error-rate, node memory).

Escalations and communications:
- Notified Product Ops and Support (via shared Slack thread) at 18:25 PDT with a short customer impact note; suggested support message template for customers seeing 5xx/timeouts.
- No legal/compliance escalation required.

Open follow-ups (owners/due):
- POST-1: Investigate why cache_shards change was rolled with no canary gating — owner: Priya Singh — due: 2028-03-31. (Linked: SRE-4521)
- POST-2: Implement autoscaler hysteresis improvements (increase scale_down_delay default, add rate limiter) — owner: Luca Morales (infra) — due: 2028-04-07.
- POST-3: Add automated smoke test that simulates worker rehydrate under burst to CI job (runtime team) — owner: Ethan Park — due: 2028-04-05.
- POST-4: Update runbook KV Cache section with the commands/snippets above and include rollback checklist — owner: Maya Chen — due: 2028-03-31.
- POST-5: Customer outreach package draft for impacted customers (CS + comms) — owner: Priya Singh — due: 2028-03-30.

Notes for next shift / watchlist:
- Monitor p95 in us-west-2 for the next 12 hours (alert profile: hosted-p95-latency, mute applied for false-positive cooldown until 08:00 PDT).
- Watch kv_cache_hit_ratio and worker_rehydrate_duration 99th.
- Keep autoscaler scale_down_delay at 300s until infra PR lands and passes canary.
- If p95 creeps >1s again: escalate to infra oncall immediately and consider traffic shaping to lower-request-size tenants.

Questions unresolved / things to validate:
- Is the cache_shards default change actually beneficial at high concurrency? Need a perf matrix per shard count vs typical request sizes.
- Why did autoscaler choose to scale-down during a traffic ramp? (logs indicate config TTL mismatch between policy and controller).
- Were any customer-specific deployments impacted differently? CS will provide a list from support tickets and we'll map to node allocation.

Appendix (useful links & queries):
- Confluence: Runbook KV Cache: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+KV+Cache
- Grafana: hosted-api-us-west2/p95 + kv_cache_hit_ratio dashboard link (internal)
- Jira: SRE-4521 (cache rollout postmortem)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/834 (cache_shards rollback PR)
- Slack thread: slack:/C07SREXYZ/thread/Arq9g2f4

Quick TL;DR for next oncall: rollback fixed the visible spike — followups required on rollout gating and autoscaler hysteresis. Keep an eye on rehydrate durations and be ready to revert autoscaler changes if memory pressure grows.

Ethan: CI smoke test for rehydrate, due 2028-04-05
Maya: update runbook KV Cache section, due 2028-03-31
